encoder: legalese: a single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from the brief (no ontology agent, no fleet, no independent test author while it was written; one was added afterwards, see independent_review, no subagents)
display_name: Swiss Federal Supreme Court Act (BGG, SR 173.110), chapter 4: the appeal procedure (Art. 90 to 112), wired to chapter 3
seat: a person affected by a decision (a party to civil or criminal proceedings, or to proceedings in a public-law matter, who lost, or a person with another interest the text names), asking on facts they can state which decisions they may appeal, on what grounds, by when, what new submissions are allowed, whether the appeal stops the decision from taking effect, and what the cantons must provide

scope.encoded: Art. 90 to 112 (4. Kapitel, Beschwerdeverfahren, seven sections), every Article, paragraph, list item and sentence row of the coverage table, wired to the read-only chapter 3 modules in bgg4-seams
scope.not_encoded: the rules outside the sources, asked as inputs: how time limits run, are suspended and are restored, the value in dispute, the parties (the brief places them in chapter 2); Art 42(2), Art 48(3), Art 58(1)(b); the Patent Act and the two conventions named in Art 100(2)(c), (d); the federal and cantonal law of Art 112(2); the Federal Council determination of Art 112(4)
scope.edition: Fedlex consolidated version in German applicable from 2026-04-01, as a plain-text rendering made by a converter script (not the official text), ch-bgg-sr173110-ch4-art-90-112-20260401.txt, 166 lines, sha256 57b31040c47e38955d09531f374082497e4d38becfce47e28bcff1173fc5a8d3

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the text, and the text file is a script rendering of the consolidated version, not the official text; nothing here is verified against the official text.
